items.question: Bioavailability of a drug given intravenously is?
items.explanation: IV route bypasses absorption, so bioavailability (F) is 100% by definition.

items.question: Zero-order kinetics means a constant ______ is eliminated per unit time.
items.explanation: In zero-order kinetics a constant AMOUNT is eliminated per unit time (e.g., ethanol, phenytoin at high dose).

items.question: Zero-order elimination becomes important for phenytoin because at therapeutic doses enzymes are?
items.explanation: Phenytoin shows saturation (Michaelis-Menten) kinetics; small dose increases cause large plasma rises.

items.question: Flip-flop kinetics occurs when?
options: Absorption rate is slower than elimination
items.explanation: In flip-flop kinetics the slow absorption rate governs the terminal slope (e.g., depot/SR formulations).

items.question: Levothyroxine absorption is reduced by concurrent?
items.explanation: Calcium and iron bind levothyroxine, reducing absorption; separate dosing is needed.

*PharmaCraft Daily - 11 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Bioavailability of a drug given intravenously is?
Ans: 100%
Why: IV route bypasses absorption, so bioavailability (F) is 100% by definition.

🌍 *FMGE* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Zero-order kinetics means a constant ______ is eliminated per unit time.
Ans: amount
Why: In zero-order kinetics a constant AMOUNT is eliminated per unit time (e.g., ethanol, phenytoin at high dose).

🩺 *NEET PG* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Zero-order elimination becomes important for phenytoin because at therapeutic doses enzymes are?
Ans: Saturated
Why: Phenytoin shows saturation (Michaelis-Menten) kinetics; small dose increases cause large plasma rises.

🏥 *INI-CET* (General Pharmacology)
Q: Flip-flop kinetics occurs when?
Ans: Absorption rate is slower than elimination
Why: In flip-flop kinetics the slow absorption rate governs the terminal slope (e.g., depot/SR formulations).

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper III: Systemic)
Q: Levothyroxine absorption is reduced by concurrent?
Ans: Calcium/iron supplements
Why: Calcium and iron bind levothyroxine, reducing absorption; separate dosing is needed.
